explanation: Track used digits for every row, column and subgrid. Repeatedly choose an empty cell with the fewest legal candidates, try each candidate, and undo failed choices. Only initially empty cells are assigned, preserving clues.
timeComplexity: Exponential search: at most O(n^e) branches for e empty cells on an n by n board, with O(n³) candidate scanning per search node. Each recursive choice fills an empty cell, giving at most n choices at each of e branching levels; the local candidate-check cost multiplies that tree size.
spaceComplexity: O(n² + en) auxiliary space for the used-digit tables and up to n retained candidate choices in each of e recursive frames. Each live recursive call and retained candidate structure is counted; the board itself belongs to the caller.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract; EPI problem attribution remains in the collection.
correctness: The row, column and subgrid tables describe exactly the digits already placed. Every attempted candidate is absent from all three relevant tables, so each placement preserves Sudoku validity and every original clue remains untouched. Failed branches undo both the cell and its table entries. Trying every legal candidate is complete: any valid completion must choose one of them. The fewest-candidates heuristic changes only search order, not which completions are possible.
walkthrough: Start with [[1, 0, 0, 4], [0, 4, 1, 0], [0, 1, 4, 0], [4, 0, 0, 1]]. Try 2 at row 0, column 1; row 0 then forces 3 in column 2. The top-left block forces 3 at (1, 0), followed by 2 at (1, 3). Continuing gives [[1, 2, 3, 4], [3, 4, 1, 2], [2, 1, 4, 3], [4, 3, 2, 1]]. Every clue is preserved and every unit is valid; the adapter returns true.
edgeCases: A fully solved board requires no assignments.
Subgrid width is the square root of the valid board dimension, including 4 by 4 boards.
Only zero cells are changed; a dead-end branch must undo its tentative digit before trying another.
